observations: Photo 0: A disassembled metal engine sub-assembly (oil pump/balance shaft housing) resting on a dirty concrete floor, with a visible gear set (one gear appears bronze/brass colored) and several long threaded rods passed through the casting.
Photo 0: Another engine component (possibly a timing cover or block section) visible in the background, not part of the item for sale.
Photo 1: A hand holds the same assembly, showing two round bearing/journal bores - likely where the balance shafts seat.
Photo 2: Close-up of the casting showing multiple bolt holes, a casting mark reading '5-B', and a mounting flange. No Toyota logo, part number, or OEM sticker is legible.
The long threaded rods running through the housing in photos 0 and 1 look like generic bolts or alignment studs, not clearly original fasteners.
Surfaces show grime, light surface oxidation, and handling wear consistent with a used, pulled part rather than new stock.

identity.kind: engine oil pump / balance shaft assembly (used, pulled part)
read_from: photo 2 casting mark '5-B' (not a decodable Toyota part number)

claims.evidence: No part number, casting number, or Toyota logo legible in any photo to cross-check against Camry fitment charts.
Same as above; no identifying marks visible in photos 0-2.

claims.claim: Implied working/good condition (by virtue of being listed for sale)
claims.evidence: No photo or video shows the shaft spinning freely, the pump priming, or gear backlash being checked.

risks.risk: Internal wear or damage to balance shaft bearings/journals (scoring, play, seizure) not visible from static photos.
risks.proof: Video clip of the balance shafts/gears being hand-rotated showing smooth, free movement with no grinding or excess play.
risks.if_unproven: priced as worn/not verified functional, i.e. core/rebuild-grade condition

risks.risk: Oil pump internals (rotor, relief valve) could be worn or the pump could be non-functional.
risks.proof: Photo of the pump's internal rotor/gerotor removed from its cover, or a bench pressure/flow test clip.

risks.risk: Fitment mismatch: part may belong to a different generation, engine code, or model despite seller's claim.
risks.proof: Clear photo of a stamped casting/part number (e.g., Toyota OEM number like 13510-XXXXX) matched against Camry/RAV4 parts catalog.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic/unconfirmed fitment, not guaranteed Camry 2018+/RAV4 specific

risks.risk: Missing components: gaskets, seals, sprocket/chain, or sensor that normally ship with this assembly may not be included.
risks.proof: A full top-down photo laid out with all included parts and fasteners counted.
risks.if_unproven: priced as bare housing only, without ancillary parts

risks.risk: The long threaded rods through the casting may be the seller's own alignment tools and not included with the sale, or could indicate the casting was cracked and is being held/clamped.
risks.proof: Photo with the rods removed showing the housing intact and bolt holes empty.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming rods are not included and housing integrity is unconfirmed

proof_requests: Close-up photo of any stamped part/casting number on the housing, readable and in focus.
Video of the balance shaft gears being rotated by hand to show smoothness and absence of play or grinding.
Photo with the long rods/tools removed to show the bare housing and confirm no cracks.
Full top-down photo of all included parts and fasteners laid out together.
response.reason: The item is clearly a used Toyota-style oil pump/balance shaft housing by type, but no legible part number confirms exact model fitment and no functional test is shown, so it must be priced at worst case as an unverified, possibly worn, bare assembly pending the listed proofs.
